html:
Ritual killing of people as offerings to the gods, central to the religion of the Mexica, the Aztecs of Tenochtitlan, in the 1400s and early 1500s.

The Mexica believed the gods had given their own blood to make the world, and that the sun and the earth had to be fed in return. The main victims were war captives, many taken in ritual "flower wars" against neighbours such as Tlaxcala. Priests killed them on the pyramid platforms, above all at the Templo Mayor, which was rededicated in 1487 under the ruler ahuitzotl. Skulls were set on public racks. Archaeologists have found one near the temple.

The Spanish wrote of 20,000 or even 80,000 victims at that 1487 festival. Historians think such numbers are far too high, but they agree the practice was real and large.

It helped the Spanish. Subject peoples hated the tribute and the captive-taking, and joined Cortes against the Mexica. The Spanish also used it to justify the conquest.
sum: Ritual killing of people as offerings to the gods, central to the religion of the Mexica, the Aztecs of Tenochtitlan, in the 1400s and early 1500s.
